expect: A radioactive tracer used in a PET scan has a half-life of 110 minutes. A patient is given a dose at 9:00 am. Calculate how many half-lives will have passed by 3:40 pm and determine what fraction of the original activity remains at that time. Show all working.
value: A radioactive tracer has a half-life of 110 minutes. A patient is given a dose at 9:00 am. Calculate how many half-lives have passed by 2:30 pm and state what fraction of the original activity is left at that time. Show all working.
note: F16: 9:00 am to 3:40 pm is 400 minutes, which is 3.64 half-lives. P5.1.11 limits this calculation to a whole number of half-lives, so the time is moved to 2:30 pm, which is exactly 3 half-lives.

expect: Time elapsed = 3:40 pm − 9:00 am = 6 hours 40 minutes = 400 minutes (1). Number of half-lives = 400 ÷ 110 = 3.636... ≈ 3.64 half-lives (1). For a clean integer check: 3 half-lives = 330 min; fraction remaining after 3 full half-lives = 1/8 (accept any correct working for partial half-lives). Award full marks for consistent method: fraction = (0.5)^(400/110) ≈ 0.079 (1). Correct final fraction stated with units or as a decimal (1). Note: both approaches (exact or integer approximation with clear working) are acceptable.
value:
Time elapsed = 2:30 pm − 9:00 am = 5 hours 30 minutes = 330 minutes (1). Number of half-lives = 330 ÷ 110 = 3 (1). Fraction left = ½ × ½ × ½ = 1/8 (1). So one eighth, or 0.125, of the original activity is left (1).

Common error: dividing the total time by the activity instead of counting the halvings.
note: F16: the old key also gave (0.5)^(400/110) as 0.079 when it is 0.080, and asked for units on a fraction, which has none. Recomputed key for the whole number of half-lives.
F16: giving the net decline as a ratio after a whole number of half-lives is P5.1.11, which is bold, so the question is Higher only.
